question: A patient with chronic pain is not on opioids; optimized non-opioid treatment has not been effective, but the patient is not able or willing to engage in a comprehensive pain care plan. Per the VA/DoD opioid algorithm, should opioids be started?
assumption: Assuming the VA/DoD Opioids CPG (2022, v4.0) Module A algorithm.
answer:
**No. Don't start opioids.**

Module A path for an opioid-naïve patient:
1. Non-opioid treatment is optimized but ineffective (Box 6 = No).
2. Complete the opioid risk assessment and refer for interdisciplinary and specialty consults (Box 7).
3. If benefits outweigh risks (Box 8 = Yes), refer for interdisciplinary treatments (Box 9).
4. Box 10 asks whether the patient is able and willing to engage in a comprehensive pain care plan. The answer here is **No**, so the algorithm goes to Box 17: **exit the algorithm and manage with non-opioid modalities**.

Opioids are only considered after Box 10 is "Yes". Module B starts from a candidate "in conjunction with a comprehensive pain care plan".

va_dod_cpg_opioids_2022 (VA, advisory, 2022-05)
VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for the Use of Opioids in the Management of Chronic Pain (Version 4.0) > VIII. Algorithm > B. Module B: Initiation of Treatment with Opioids
[p 26]
[Figure, flowchart] untitled in the image; see the section heading (PDF page 26). Machine-generated visual interpretation; status: machine-interpreted from the page image by a vision model; compared box by box against the page image (not clinician-verified).
Box 18 (start): Candidate for opioids with consent (begin a trial in conjunction with comprehensive pain care plan) -> then box 19
Box 19 (action): Initiate opioids using the following approach: • Use short duration (e.g., 1-week initial prescription) • Plan to reevaluate at 30 days or fewer • Use lowest effective dose, recognizing that no dose is completely safe ▪ A strategy of escalating dose to achieve benefit increases risk (see Sidebar L) and has not been shown to improve function • Long-acting opioids should not be prescribed for opioid-naïve individuals (see Recommendation 11 and Appendix D) • Consider alternatives to methadone and transdermal fentanyl (see Appendix D) • Assess improvement in pain and functional status and adverse effects • Complete risk mitigation strategies (see Sidebar E) • Provide medication and overdose education, offer naloxone prescription -> then box 20
Box 20 (action): Reevaluation as needed clinically and based on patient risk factors (e.g., 1-4 weeks after initiation of opioids, not later than 30 days) • Assess: ▪ Function, pain, risks, and benefits of opioids ▪ Adverse effects ▪ Adherence to treatment plan ▪ Complications or co-occurring conditions (e.g., medical, behavioral health, and/or SUD) ▪ Patient preference • Complete risk mitigation strategies (see Sidebar E) • Review and optimize comprehensive pain care plan (e.g., non-opioid treatments, self-management strategies) -> then box 21
Box 21 (decision): Does the patient want to continue opioid therapy? -> if No: box 22; if Yes: box 23
Box 22 (action): • Taper to discontinuation (consult Module C if needed) • Manage with non-opioid modalities
Box 23 (decision): Is there clinically meaningful improvement in function and pain that outweighs risks? -> if No: box 22; if Yes: box 24
Box 24 (decision): Is the patient sufficiently medically and behaviorally stable to continue opioid medication? -> if No: box 25; if Yes: box 26
Box 25 (action): Provide medical and/or behavioral health treatment to stabilize as indicated; consider tapering opioids to discontinuation (consult Module C)
Box 26 (decision): Are there factors that increase risks of opioids (e.g., non-adherence, co-occurring conditions, indications of OUD)? -> if Yes: box 27; if No: box 28
Box 27 (action): Consider one or more of the following: • Shortening prescribing interval • Intensifying risk mitigation strategies (see Sidebar E) • Referring to interdisciplinary care • Consulting with or referring to specialty care • Switching to partial agonist opioids • See VA/DoD SUD CPG if there are indications of OUD* -> then box 29
Box 28 (action): Reassess in 1-3 months or more frequently as determined by patient risk factors (see Sidebar G) -> then box 20
Box 29 (decision): Are there indications to discontinue or taper? (see Sidebar F) -> if No: box 28; if Yes: box 30
Box 30 (end): Taper to reduced dose or taper to discontinuation; proceed to Module C

Decision path: 18 -> 19 -> 20 -> 21 -> [Yes] 23 -> [No] 22
Decision path: 18 -> 19 -> 20 -> 21 -> [Yes] 23 -> [Yes] 24 -> [No] 25
Decision path: 18 -> 19 -> 20 -> 21 -> [Yes] 23 -> [Yes] 24 -> [Yes] 26 -> [Yes] 27 -> 29 -> [No] 28 -> back to box 20
Decision path: 18 -> 19 -> 20 -> 21 -> [Yes] 23 -> [Yes] 24 -> [Yes] 26 -> [Yes] 27 -> 29 -> [Yes] 30
Decision path: 18 -> 19 -> 20 -> 21 -> [Yes] 23 -> [Yes] 24 -> [Yes] 26 -> [No] 28 -> back to box 20
Abbreviations: OUD: opioid use disorder; SUD: substance use disorders; VA/DoD SUD CPG: VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Substance Use Disorders
